patterns: is north always up on a map
entries.answer: North is the direction along the axis the Earth turns on, and it is fixed by the pole rather than by anything on the ground. Almost every map places it at the top, which is a convention and not a fact, and a few cultures have done the opposite for centuries. The word is also the ordinary term for a region, as in the far north, and it survives in the names of countries whose borders were drawn by people who thought in terms of it.

entries.answer: South is the direction opposite north and towards the other pole, and the word is common well outside the places where anyone actually navigates by it. It is associated both with cold, as a compass point, and with heat, as a region, so the two senses pull in opposite directions and the context decides. In navigation it also names crossing a latitude in that direction, which is how one would say we went south of the border.

patterns: is east the direction of sunrise
entries.answer: East is the direction of sunrise and the one on the right when you are facing north, which makes it a relationship rather than a fixed location. The word is older as the name of a region than as a point of the compass, and the two uses are still distinct, so a country in the far east need not lie east of anywhere in particular. Going east means moving the way the Earth spins, and that is the only sense of it that is not arbitrary.

entries.answer: West is the last of the four main points and the one the word most often means as a region rather than a direction, since the West has named a cultural bloc for a long time. In navigation it is the direction of sunset and the left when facing north. The associations are mixed, because the word carries decline as readily as romance, and neither of those is geographical at all but both are firmly attached to the name.

entries.answer: A compass finds direction with a magnetised needle, and the word also names the whole set of points the instrument reports. The needle points roughly north because the Earth's field is itself magnetic, which is why it behaves badly near steel and why declination has to be allowed for in a reading. A compass rose on a map shows the same set, and the tradition of drawing east at the top came from putting it there on the instrument.

entries.answer: A cardinal direction is one of the four main points, north, south, east and west, as against the intercardinal ones lying between them. The word comes from a Latin term for hinge, because these four are the hinges everything else turns between. The opposite, an ordinal direction, is numbered from north, so north-north-east is the first of those. Memorising the eight is quicker than deriving them, and deriving them is where people usually go wrong.
